summary: Where the current page sits in the hierarchy — every level but the last is a link.

pairs.dont: Make the last crumb a link to the page you are already on.
pairs.do: Render it as the current page, with aria-current.
pairs.why: A link that goes nowhere wastes a tab stop and tells a screen-reader user the wrong thing about where they are.

pairs.dont: Print all seven levels and let the row wrap.
pairs.do: Collapse the middle into an ellipsis past four levels.
pairs.why: The first and last levels are what people orient by. The middle is only needed when someone goes looking.

pairs.dont: Show where the person has been.
pairs.do: Show where this page sits in the structure.
pairs.why: Breadcrumbs describe the hierarchy, not the journey. A trail that changes per visitor cannot be learned.

pairs.dont: Leave the collapsed crumb as three dots and nothing else.
pairs.do: Give it text only a screen reader hears.
pairs.why: An ellipsis is a shape. Without words it is a control nobody can name or explain.

pairs.dont: Reach for sm expecting smaller text in a dense context.
pairs.do: Use sm to tighten the gaps — both sizes are body/md at 14px.
pairs.why: Size moves the spacing only. If the type needs to shrink, that is a change to make in Figma first.

a11y: The <nav> carries aria-label="Breadcrumb". That is what distinguishes it from every other nav on the page.
The current page takes aria-current="page" and is not a link.
Separators and the ellipsis glyph are aria-hidden, so the trail reads as a list of names rather than "slash" between each one.
The ellipsis ships an sr-only label, "Show hidden levels" by default. Replace the text, not the mechanism.
